incident-bot: PAGER -> oncall @Sam O'Neill: High error rate on /v1/generate (5xx spike). Detected at 03:41 UTC. Auto-mitigations kicked: scaled serving pool by 2x and routed new traffic to region-us-west-2. Please ack and investigate. :rotating_light:
Sam O'Neill: Acked. jumping in now.
Sam O'Neill: quick check — 5xxs look like memory-related OOMs from the runtime process on nodes tagged model-serving-*. stack traces show repeated `std::bad_alloc` on tokenization path.
Dmitri Kozlov: I'm looking at the kernel change from yesterday (runtime-ops commit fa3b1). That change tweaks the attention kernel heuristics for >4k context. Rolling it back on a small canary now.
Sam O'Neill: Thanks. Canary rollback started. Logs: ```
kubectl -n serving rollout undo deploy/runtime-serving --to-revision=fa3b0
redwoodctl pool scale --name=interactive-serving --replicas=60
```
Priyanka Rao: ETA on rollback completion? Also need customer impact numbers before we escalate.
Sam O'Neill: Rollback finished at 03:54 UTC. Error rate dropped from 6.8% -> 0.5% within 4m. Tail latency normalized.
Maya Gupta: From observability — ~0.8% of production requests experienced 500s for ~13 minutes. Two paying customers (acme-inc, beta-shop) saw a noticeable spike; we already have a handful of dropped requests in the metrics. No data exfiltration.
Leah Chen: Thanks. Sam can you capture the minimal reproduction or logs we need for root cause? I'll take the post-incident follow-ups; I'm on at 09:00 UTC for handoff.
Sam O'Neill: Minimal repro: long-context (>6k tokens) + quantized weights + runtime kernel=heuristic-v2. Repro script attached below: ```
# repro snippet
python tools/repro.py --model redwood-7b --context 8000 --profile
```
Dmitri Kozlov: Confirmed the heuristic picks a vectorized kernel that increases mem footprint in specific quantization layout — triggers under long sequences. Short-term: rollback in prod (done). Medium-term: add safety fallback in kernel selector + tests.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 04:02 UTC (auto). Incident ID: INF-4321. Please open a postmortem and assign owners for action items.
Leah Chen: Scheduling: propose postmortem tomorrow 11:00 UTC (60m). Invite: eng-runtime, eng-ml, eng-sre, product, customer-success. Thoughts?
Maya Gupta: +1. Suggest we include a line in the PM note for customer comms and flag any customers to personally reach out to. 
Priyanka Rao: I'll add a monitoring runbook update and set a permanent alert for this pattern.
Sam O'Neill: I'll open the postmortem draft and link INF-4321 -> INF-4322 for action tracking. PRD link placeholder: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4322
Leah Chen: Action item creation (initial triage) — let's size and prioritize based on severity and customer impact. We flagged this as Sev2 (service interruption for a subset of requests; no PII). Mapping: Sev1->P0, Sev2->P1, Sev3->P2. This is Sev2 -> P1. We'll propose Q2 tie-in for reliability epic.
--- Proposed action items (from thread):
1) Kernel selector safe-fallback (owner: Dmitri Kozlov) — description: implement defensive fallback when mem growth detected, add unit/integration tests for quantized layouts. size: 8d (medium). priority: P1 -> include in Q2 reliability sprint.
2) Add regression test harness for long-context quantized paths (owner: Sam O'Neill) — description: automated repro added to CI, nightly smoke. size: 3d (small). priority: P1 -> backlog groom for Q2 sprint 1.
3) Monitoring & alerting (owner: Priyanka Rao) — description: new alert rule for abrupt delta in 5xx% tied to kernel change, and dashboard for impacted customers. size: 2d (small). priority: P1 -> quick win, target next week.
4) Customer comms & post-incident notes (owner: Maya Gupta / CS) — description: send status + RCA when PM ready, follow-up for affected customers. size: 1d (small). priority: P1 -> coordinate with legal if needed.
5) Dedicated canary runs for runtime kernel changes (owner: Leah Chen / eng-sre) — description: expand canary matrix to include long-context quantized workloads. size: 10d (large) — plan for Q2 epic. priority: P0/P1 (depending on resource) -> propose part of Dedicated reliability OKR.
6) Rollout policy improvement (owner: Product engineer TBD) — description: automatic staged rollouts with telemetry gates (fail fast). size: 5d (medium). priority: P1 -> tie to Q2 rollout automation.
---
Sam O'Neill: I'll create the JIRA tasks with the above owners and estimates right after this thread. INF-4323..INF-4328 will map to the items.
Dmitri Kozlov: For the kernel item, estimate assumes 2 engineers focused; if it's one person it'll take longer. Flagging dependency: needs perf infra changes from eng-infra (ticket INF-4390).
Priyanka Rao: I'll update the oncall runbook with step-by-step mitigation commands and add the new alert thresholds. Will link runbook PR in the postmortem.
Maya Gupta: I'll draft customer comms after the postmortem draft is in good shape. For the two affected customers, we should offer a 2-week prioritized support window.
Leah Chen: Handoff notes for next oncall: incident resolved, root cause prelim: kernel-selector regression under long-context quantized workload. Open action items (P1/P0) assigned as above. Postmortem scheduled: tomorrow 11:00 UTC. Owners: Dmitri, Sam, Priyanka, Maya.
ops-rotations-bot: Reminder added to oncall calendar: @Leah Chen will be primary for postmortem and follow-ups.
Sam O'Neill: One more: can we please tag this to Q2 planning board under "Reduce tail latency / Reliable kernels" so PMs can prioritize? If Leah or product can do that, great.
Leah Chen: I'll add it to the Q2 planning doc and raise it in the fortnightly triage sync.
Maya Gupta: Thanks everyone. Action owners — please update the JIRA tickets with real estimates by EOD tomorrow so we can slot into Q2 planning.
Sam O'Neill: Closing my oncall handoff now — leaving notes in INF-4322. Leah, I'll ping you in the morning for any last context.
Leah Chen: thanks Sam. I'll run the postmortem and post the final RCA with action items and owners. Expect a follow-up thread after the meeting with SOC/CS notes. :pray:
